newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Democrats oppose woodchip plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Democrats oppose woodchip plan.

text.p: Australian Democrats environment spokeswoman Meg Lees said on Monday it would not support the government's new woodchip export regulations which allow an additional million tonnes of woodchip exports this year.
"The government's new set of regulations are an appalling con and the thought of a return to the free-for-all days of individual licences is also horrendous," Lees said in a statement.
"This is another case of a federal government being played like a puppet by the voracious and insatiable short term logging industry," she said.
Lees said the Democrats would support the Australian Greens motion to disallow new export regulations, being debated in the upper house, the Senate, late on Monday.
The Labor opposition said earlier on Monday it would also support the disallowance motion.
The passage of the motion requires a majority of senators, Labor and the Democrats would need the support of two Independent senators to disallow the regulations.
Neither Independents have indicated which way they will vote.
The Liberal-National government last week approved five more export licences for 1996 against the Greens' motion, allowing 415,000 tonnes of chips from native forests.
The government said in July under the new export licencing regime exporters would have access to an additional one million tonnes of woodchips sourced exclusively from sawmill residues in 1996.
Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said the ceiling of 5.251 million tonnes applying to all woodchips would continue.
Lees said: "Under the new regulation there would have been no real ceiling on woodchips for export as they allowed unlimited tonnage under degraded forest licences on private land."
Under the new regulations the first and second-stage licences would also be abolished with three-year licences available from 1997.
